fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the main residence and detached structure.
• Mark or label the detached structure on any posted site map or address sign so responders can identify multiple structures on arrival.
• Trim vegetation near the main residence and detached structure to maintain clear walking paths around all exterior walls.
• Keep a gate, gap, or clear path at the rear of the property unlocked and accessible so responders can reach the rear without returning to the front.
• Mark the rear access point with a reflective indicator visible from inside the property so responders can locate it quickly.
• Keep the utility area clear of stored items so responders can identify and reach utility shutoffs without obstruction.
• Trim any vegetation that blocks sightlines between the front access drive and the detached structure.
• Keep the patio area clear of furniture or objects that would block movement along the side or rear of the residence.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim any shrubs that have grown close to the base of the house or outbuildings.
• Keep grass around structures mowed short, especially during dry months.
• Remove dead grass and dried plant material that has accumulated near the foundation.
• Thin scattered trees near structures so their branches do not touch or overhang the roofline.
• Keep low-hanging branches on trees near the house trimmed up from the ground.
• Clear any dried grass or loose debris from gutters and along the base of exterior walls.
• Keep driveways and access routes clear of overhanging branches that could block emergency vehicle access.
• Separate any wood piles, patio furniture, or other stored materials from the exterior walls of structures.
